Subject: Multi-year prepay — ramp schedule & true-up buffer band clarification

Hi Dana,

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is the v3 term sheet reflecting the 3-year prepay we discussed: 40% year 1 / 30% year 2 / 30% year 3 (billed annually), with a suggested 10% buffer band and an end-of-term reconciliation true-up.

Two quick notes I wanted to call out so we’re aligned before we get legal involved:
- Ramp schedule: the invoice and credit cadence we propose is annual billing at the start of each year, with the ability to reallocate unused committed units forward once per year at the start of the subsequent term.
- True-up / buffer band: the standard we’re proposing is a +/-10% buffer band on committed tokens for year-level usage. Usage within that band is considered covered by the prepay. Overages beyond +10% are billed at the overage rate (80% of list per-token rate) and at the end-of-term we reconcile cumulative usage against cumulative prepay. If the customer under-consumes by more than 10% we offer a one-time carry-forward or a partial credit per the term sheet.

Please review the attached term sheet and let me know if you want a tighter buffer (we can propose 5%) or a tiered overage (e.g., 10-20% at 90% of list, 20%+ at 100% of list). Once we lock the approach we’ll provide redline language for procurement.

Best,
Rishi

Rishi —

Thanks for the doc. A couple of things procurement flagged as they evaluate the commercial model:

1) Buffer band math — Procurement wants an example showing how the reconciliation works in practice across a 3-year term. Specifically: if our actual usage in Year 1 is 55% of Year-1 committed tokens because our product team delays a feature, do we lose that prepay? Or can we shift to Year 2?

2) Overage caps — They asked whether we can cap annual overage charges so we don’t get a surprise invoice that’s multiple x the prepay in a single quarter. Can we provide a quarterly cap (e.g., max 40% of annual committed units billed as overage per quarter) or an annual cap?

3) Audit and reporting — They asked for the reporting cadence and a confirmation that monthly usage reports (CSV) will be available and mutually agreed metrics used for reconciliation.

We’re generally favorable to the prepay approach — they just want the guardrails spelled out. Could you propose 2 variant options we can evaluate: 
A) More conservative customer-friendly: 5% buffer band, ability to shift up to 30% of unused Year-1 commitment to Year-2, annual overage cap at 25% of committed units, and monthly CSV exports.
B) Commercially-favorable: 10% buffer band, one-time carry-forward of unused Year-1 up to 15% of committed units, overage billed at 80% list with no quarterly cap (but aggregate annual reconciliation).

If you can put these in redline language we can move to legal review quickly.

Thanks — Dana
Director, Cloud Procurement | Acme Corp

Rishi —

Suggested approach (practical + low legal friction):

Option 1 — Customer-friendly (recommended if Acme is price-sensitive and uncertain usage):
- Buffer band: +/-5% per-contract-year.
- Carry-forward: up to 30% of Year-N unused committed units may be applied to Year-(N+1) if requested within 60 days of Year-N close; remaining unused units expire.
- Overage cap: Annual cap at 25% of the contracted annual commitment; overages within each quarter billed monthly but credits applied at year-end reconciliation so no single quarter exceeds the cap in net.
- Reporting: Monthly CSV exports with month-to-date and rolling 12-month totals; audit rights limited to quarterly samples unless material discrepancy (>5%) detected.

Option 2 — Commercial (recommended if we maintain margin):
- Buffer band: +/-10% per-contract-year.
- Carry-forward: one-time carry-forward of up to 15% of Year-N unused to Year-(N+1), applies automatically unless otherwise specified.
- Overage: Billed at 80% of list for usage beyond buffer; annual reconciliation to true-up and issue invoice/credit. No guaranteed quarterly cap.

Redline suggestions to send to Acme: provide both options in the term sheet; include a worked example appendix showing a 3-year reconciliation (numbers). For caps, we can offer the customer-friendly cap as a limited concession linked to signature by Feb 15, 2026.

I drafted quick redline language and a reconciliation example in the attached doc — feel free to edit before sending.

-Lauren
